reason: This passage (2 Kings 18-19) describes the Assyrian invasion under Sennacherib and God's response through the prophet Isaiah. The text contains Yahweh's promise of protection and deliverance, not a complaint about the people. While the Rabshakeh's speech mentions Hezekiah's religious reforms, this is an enemy's taunt, not divine complaint. God's response to Hezekiah's prayer is one of reassurance and military intervention on behalf of Jerusalem, culminating in the miraculous destruction of the Assyrian army. There is no expression of divine displeasure or complaint directed toward Judah or Jerusalem in this account.
